title: Staged deployment & signal runbook for rollouts
content:
Purpose: This working doc defines a cross-functional operational playbook for staged deployments: canaries, small-scale bakeoffs, and A/B experiments for the Redwood inference platform. It focuses on practical signal definitions, owners, ramp schedules, and kill/rollback criteria so product, SRE, infra, DS, and customer success can run predictable, low-risk rollouts for model, config, and infra changes.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to: model version rollouts, runtime config changes (batching/quantization), routing policy updates, and console/route changes that affect production inference traffic.
- Not covered here: full research experiment design (see DS experiment templates) or legal/compliance approvals (see security-and-compliance).

Cross-functional roles (who does what):
- Product rollout lead (PRL) — coordinates stakeholders, approves ramping schedule, owns communication.
- SRE / Infra lead — responsible for capacity, autoscaling config, and operational runbook execution (kill/fallback).
- Data Science / Quality lead — defines quality/regression metrics, supplies evaluation prompt-set and acceptance criteria.
- Observability / Monitoring owner (Console team) — builds/validates dashboards, alerting, traces for the rollout.
- Solutions / Customer Success — identifies impacted customers and coordinates outreach if we detect regressions.
- On-call engineers — execute alerts, apply hotfixes, and run rollback.

Phases of a typical rollout (recommended default cadence):
1) Local verification & preflight (dev/staging) — PRL sign-off; smoke tests & unit level checks.
2) Canary 1 (internal-only, 0.5–2% traffic or 2 nodes) — fast health check for obvious regressions and infra stability. Run for 30–90 minutes minimum (longer for low-frequency routes).
3) Canary 2 (expanded internal or pilot customers, 5–10% traffic) — evaluate primary business and quality signals; run for at least 2–12 hours depending on volume.
4) Bakeoff / A/B (50/50 split for experiment) — statistically powered A/B test for final KPI verification (if applicable).
5) Ramp to 25/50/75/100% — controlled increments with quick checks at each step and mandatory hold windows.

Traffic ramp guidance:
- Default step increments: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% (adjust for route volume).
- Minimum hold times: small steps (0.5–2%): 30–90m; medium steps (2–25%): 2–6h; large steps: 12–24h.
- For low-volume routes (fewer than 1000 reqs/day), prefer node-based canaries (single instance) and longer hold times.

Signal taxonomy (what to watch):
A) Service health & infra signals (SRE primary):
- p95/p99 latency (generation time) — relative change > +25% is high risk.
- error rate (5xx, model runtime errors) — absolute increase > 0.5% or relative x3 baseline triggers immediate attention.
- queue/backlog length and CPU/GPU utilization — sustained >85% GPU utilization is warning; >95% is critical.
- autoscaler events and scale failures.

B) Quality & model output signals (DS/product primary):
- regression rate on core eval prompt-set (per-prompt correctness) — threshold: > 1.5x baseline or +3 percentage points.
- hallucination proxy (fuzzy-match to ground truths) — configurable per-model; default alert if degradation > 2x baseline.
- semantic drift / embedding distance drift for embedding routes.
- token-cost delta (average tokens per response) — unexpected increases may indicate hallucination or verbosity regressions.

C) Business & user-facing signals (product/customer-success primary):
- conversion funnel drop (for routes tied to revenue flows) — any statistically significant drop (p < 0.01) over hold window.
- user-reported incidents / escalations (monitored in Slack threads and CS queue).
- SLA latency breaches (percentage of requests violating SLA threshold).

D) Safety & content signals (security/compliance/DS):
- safety classifier hit-rate changes (toxicity, PII leakage classifiers) — alert on any increase beyond configurable guardrail.
- high-severity moderation flags (manual-review queue spike).

Signal aggregation & alert rules (observability):
- Create a rollout dashboard per rollout that shows: traffic fraction, p50/p95/p99, error-rate, DS regression %, safety hits, cost/tokens, GPU util.
- Define short-window rolling checks (5m, 1h) and long-window checks (3h, 24h).
- Alert severity mapping: S1 (stop & rollback) for fatal infra or large regression signals; S2 (pause + investigate) for moderate degradation; S3 (monitor) for borderline anomalies.

Statistical guidance for A/B / bakeoffs:
- Use sequential testing (e.g., sequential probability ratio test or group sequential designs) where possible to allow early stopping without inflating Type-I error.
- If using fixed-horizon tests, compute minimum sample size based on target metric: n per arm ≈ (Z_{1-α/2}+Z_{1-β})^2 * 2σ^2 / Δ^2. Use α=0.01 for production-sensitivity metrics and power 80–90%.
- Use multiple-testing correction if testing many metrics; prefer a priori primary metric.
- For low-traffic endpoints, prefer longer-duration A/Bs rather than forcing high-traffic splits.

Kill/rollback criteria (examples that mandate immediate stop):
- SRE: sustained p99 latency > 2x baseline for 30 minutes or error-rate spike > 1% absolute for 15m.
- DS/Product: primary quality regression > 3 percentage points on guard prompt-set sustained for two consecutive hold windows.
- Safety: any production-seen toxic output that bypassed classifier and led to external exposure (requires immediate rollback).
- Business: conversion funnel drop with p < 0.01 during the hold window.

Rollback mechanics (operational steps):
1) PRL declares rollback and coordinates via #rollouts Slack channel.
2) Infra: route traffic back to previous model variant / config via feature-flag or routing policy. Use pre-approved rollback playbook (GH scripts: repo/infra-rollout-helpers#42).
3) Observability: mark incident in dashboard, capture logs/trace ids, start timeline.
4) DS/Product: confirm regression and open investigation ticket with dataset artifacts.
5) Post-rollback communication to stakeholders and customers.

Feature-flag & routing recommendations:
- Use stable feature-flag keys (feature:deploy/<route>/<model_version>) and keep names in rollout spreadsheet.
- Tag each rollout with a UUID and include in request traces to correlate logs.
- Maintain an explicit fallback policy: if any route-level health check fails, traffic should immediately fall back to last stable model for that route.

Observability checklist before rollout:
- Dashboard deployed and verified with synthetic traffic.
- Alerts configured and verified on-call rotations assigned.
- End-to-end trace across API -> serving runtime -> model variant is visible.
- Postman/Smoke collection loaded with guard prompt-set for quick local checks.

A/B experiment configuration template (quick fields):
- experiment_id: short string (e.g., ab/online-infer-kvcache-202603)
- hypothesis: short sentence
- primary_metric: (name + direction: increase/decrease)
- secondary_metrics: list
- min_sample_size_per_arm: numeric or TBD
- analysis_window: hours/days
- sequential? yes/no
- owner: name
- start_date, end_date (planned)

Telemetry and artifacts to capture on any rollback:
- full request traces for a representative sample (last 1h pre-rollback).
- sampled model outputs with prompt and gold/expected output where available.
- GPU/infra metrics for the affected nodes.
- DS eval results on guard prompt-set run at time of canary.

Communication template (Slack/email) for rollout milestone messages:
- Subject: [Rollout] <route> -> <model_version> | <phase> | <owner>
- Body: one-line summary, traffic fraction, hold window length, where to view dashboard, immediate contact (PRL), and rollback criteria.

Post-release checklist & learning:
- Post-mortem for any S2+ incident within 72h.
- Collect delta in unit economics (tokens/cost) observed.
- Update guard prompt-set if new failure modes observed.
- Add runbook notes and timeline to Confluence and tag relevant Jira ticket.

Open questions / TODOs (short-term):
- [TODO] Define exact numerical thresholds for hallucination proxies per model family (owner: DS).
- [TODO] Add automated canary-synth generator to inject synthetic prompts that exercise edge-cases (owner: Observability).
- [QUESTION] Should we default to sequential testing for all production A/Bs? Tradeoffs: speed vs complexity for analysts. (PRL to decide; deadline: 2026-04-01).
- [TODO] Create small-library of prebuilt rollout dashboards to avoid last-minute setup (owner: Console team).

Appendix: quick checklist for first canary run:
1) Confirm preflight tests green.
2) Create rollout ticket and tag PRL.
3) Deploy Canary 1 at 0.5% with synthetic traffic for 30m.
4) Validate infra signals and DS guard prompt-set; run scheduled checks.
5) If green, expand to Canary 2 (5–10%) and run for recommended hold time.
6) If green, run A/B or ramp according to plan.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language here lightweight — this doc is the operational checklist, not the full experiment design manual.
- Expect iteration: thresholds will change as models/metrics stabilize.
- Reach out to Maya + Diego to schedule dry-run next Tuesday with two small routes.

End of working doc.
